_comment: Copy this to ~/.config/hestia-antideadzone/config.json and edit. JSON has no comments, so any '_xxx_help' key is documentation only and is ignored by the daemon.
_device_name_match_help: Case-insensitive substring to pick your pad if you have multiple input devices (e.g. 'Xbox', 'DualSense', '8BitDo'). Leave empty to auto-pick the first thing that looks like a gamepad. Run list-devices.py to see exact names.
_profile_help: Each of 'left'/'right' has its own settings, so the two sticks can differ. deadzone: 0-1, input ignored near center. anti_deadzone: 0-1, output floor the instant the stick leaves the deadzone -- defeats a game's own internal deadzone. curve: 1.0 linear, >1.0 more precision near center, <1.0 twitchier near center; no effect on '_unscaled' shapes. deadzone_shape: 'radial' (default -- circular, no jump, diagonals stay smooth); 'radial_unscaled' (same circle, jumps to raw magnitude at the boundary instead of ramping); 'axial' (flat per-axis deadzone -- matches games with their own per-axis deadzone, but distorts angle near the edge and needs more push at an angle than straight-on); 'axial_unscaled' (same, jumps at the boundary); 'sloped_axial' (per-axis deadzone that shrinks as the other axis nears 0 -- softens axial's angle distortion and threshold mismatch); 'sloped_axial_unscaled' (same, jumps at the boundary); 'hybrid' (radial first to smooth center noise, then sloped_axial on top for axis precision). sloped_dominance_curve (0.0-2.0+, default 1.0, only affects sloped_axial/sloped_axial_unscaled/hybrid): how much of anti_deadzone reaches the smaller axis. 1.0 = scaled down by how small that axis is (clean single-axis pushes, weaker diagonal boost). 0.0 = full floor the instant its own threshold is crossed (strong diagonal boost, but ordinary noise on the off-axis can snap it toward 45 degrees). Tune to taste.
_rescan_interval_help: Seconds between reconnect attempts while no matching controller is found. Each attempt just opens the /dev/input/event* nodes and reads capabilities -- a few ms of local syscalls -- so 1s or even lower isn't a meaningful CPU cost.
_reload_interval_help: Seconds between checks of this file's last-modified time. Lower = more responsive profile switches, higher = very slightly less overhead. 1 second is already fast enough to switch mid-game between menu screens.
_debug_sample_rate_help: Set to e.g. 30 to log every 30th stick event at DEBUG level for tuning. 0 disables.
_max_output_hz_help: Caps how often stick ABS events are sent to the virtual device, in Hz. 0 (default) = unlimited, send every shaped value as fast as the source controller reports it. Useful under Proton with a high polling rate controller (500/1000Hz) if XInput emulation buffers/lags on very frequent input -- try 250, which matches a real Xbox 360 controller. Only throttles stick axes; buttons/triggers/dpad are always sent immediately, and the most recent stick value is always eventually sent, never dropped outright.
